landing.title: One command. Your engine. Your machine.
landing.lede: Ephe runs a coding agent on your computer. You choose the engine, you approve the tools, and the files stay where they are. No account, and nothing is sent until you choose.

proof.title: Three numbers, and where they come from
proof.lede: Two are other people's measurements; the third is a count of what Ephe ships. Each line names the agent that was measured, the number of runs, and the source.
proof.agentsMdBody: With a root AGENTS.md, the median run on 124 real pull requests across 10 repositories finished 28.6% sooner and emitted 16.6% fewer output tokens. The measured agent was Codex.
proof.realmBody: A two-agent ablation (17 tasks, 288 runs) kept correctness inside a 10–15 point equivalence bound. The runs that failed failed on implementation skill; missing repository knowledge was not what broke them. That is why Ephe's guarantees sit in gates a machine runs.
proof.accountsBody: There is no account and no sign-up, and Ephe ships no model weights. Until an engine is chosen in setup, the chat stays closed and the headless commands stop with an instruction.

compare.title: Six questions that decide where your work runs
compare.lede: Other coding agents answer these in their own documentation. Below are Ephe's answers, each beside the file in this repository that proves it. No cell is filled from memory.
compare.question: Question

row.engineAnswer: You pick. A local Ollama, a remote Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Until you choose, the chat stays closed and nothing is sent.
row.accountAnswer: None. No sign-up, no login, no subscription.
row.licenseAnswer: BUSL-1.1, source-available. Each release falls to Apache 2.0 four years after it ships; production use needs a commercial licence.
row.pluginsAnswer: A directory with ephe-plugin.json: versioned, content-hashed, signed. Permission families are declared in the manifest and validated fail-closed; an installed plugin lands disabled until you enable it.
row.contextAnswer: AGENTS.md at the workspace root, plus .ephe/rules/*.md. Together they are capped at 12,000 characters (6,000 per file), and every file is provenance-marked and reported with its status.
row.verificationAnswer: The repository gates itself: a per-chunk bundle budget, a per-module coverage floor, a language gate and an architecture check. In the product, a claim stays attached to the tool result behind it.

install.title: Try it in 60 seconds
install.lede: The installer prepares Python, builds the web app and starts it at http://127.0.0.1:8765. The command names release {{version}}.
install.copyFailed: The clipboard refused. Select the line and copy it yourself.
install.windowsNote: Installation on Windows is not yet verified end to end.
install.configure: No engine is needed to start: the app opens its own setup and sends nothing until you choose one. ephe configure writes the same choice to ~/.ephe/engine.json for the terminal.
install.after: Then ephe doctor reads back the engine, the model and the server state, and ephe start --open opens the app.

migrate.title: Bring the setup you already have
migrate.lede: Coming from another coding agent? ephe import reads the setup you already have and prints a plan. Nothing is written until you add --apply, and the skills it imports land disabled until you enable them.
migrate.personaLands: ~/.ephe/persona.md — an existing persona is never overwritten
migrate.settingsLands: mapped onto Ephe settings; anything unmapped is reported and left out
migrate.engine: The engine is not imported: Ephe has no silent default, so you pick it once.
migrate.plugins: Another product's plugins have no runtime here. Their skills come over where they map to the open skill-pack format.
migrate.rules: AGENTS.md keeps its meaning, and .ephe/rules/*.md adds to it. Only AGENTS.md is read as project rules.
